newsitem.title: USA: US spot LPGs sink following bearish API data.
newsitem.headline: US spot LPGs sink following bearish API data.

text.p: U.S. spot liquefied petroleum gas prices sank in lackluster midday trade on Tuesday following the release of bearish industry data showing substantial stocks builds.
Activity remained largely light, however, apart from some panic selling in the morning by players nervous prices would drop further.
"Prices fell this morning, mostly because of the API numbers," said one Houston player, noting stronger crude oil prices Tuesday helped the LPG market find a floor midday.

In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu, Texas, traded at 35.00 cents a gallon, 0.75 cents below Monday's values. Conway, Kansas, hub also fell a half cent to 35.50/36.00 cents, with 35.75 cent parcels sold.

The price drop partly reflected monthly American Petroleum Institute data that showed a 1.2 million barrel build in total propane stocks in March. Stocks are currently 4.2 million barrels or 16 percent above year-ago levels.
Ethane stocks also showed a considerable build in the API report, rising 1 million barrels in March. Inventories are 2.1 barrels, or 12.5 percent, above year-ago levels.
In Belvieu, ethane mix cratered to 18.00 cents, 1.25 cents below Monday. Purity ethane sold for 20.00 cents, 0.75 weaker from yesterday.
Conway material was also done at 16.00 cents, a penny below Monday.
Players said that most positions for April have been covered although there were shorts in May, June and July. - ((Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk, 212 859-1631))
